questions.q: A mixture of two gasses $A$ and $B$ is kept in a vessel which is maintained at a temperature& $T$. In the vessel there are $N$ molecules each of mass $m$, of the gas $A$ and $2N$ molecules each of mass $2m$ of the gas $B$. The mean square velocity of the molecules of the gas& $B$ is& $v^{2}$ and the mean square velocity of the molecules of the gas& $A$ along the $x$ direction is $w^{2}$. The value of $\dfrac{w2}{v2}$& is
questions.solution:
Mean kinetic energy of the two types of molecules should be equal. The mean square velocity of A type molecules $= {\omega}^{2} + {\omega}^{2} + {\omega}^{2} = 3{\omega}^{2}$

Therefore, $\dfrac{1}{2}m\left(3{\omega}^{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(2m\right)v^{2}$

This gives $\dfrac{{\omega}^{2}}{v^{2}} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

questions.q: An iron rocket fragment initially at$- 100 ° C$ enters the earth's atmosphere almost horizontally and quickly fuses completely in atmospheric friction. Specific heat of iron is $0. 11kcal{kg}^{- 1} ° C^{- 1}$, its melting point is $1535 ° C$ and the latent heat of fusion is $3kcal{kg}^{- 1}$. The minimum velocity with which the fragment must have entered the atmosphere is
options:
$1. 32kms^{- 1}$
&

$2. 32kms^{- 1}$
&
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy of the fragment is changed to heat. Expressing mass m in kilograms everywher, we have

$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = \left[m\left(30\right) + m\left(\text{0.11}\right)\left(153{5}^{∘} + 10{0}^{∘}\right)\right]4184$

$v^{2} = \left(8368\right)\left[30 + 180\right] ≃ \text{1.76} \times 1{0}^{6}$

Hence

$v = \left(\sqrt{\text{1.76}}\right) \times 1{0}^{3} = {1.32 km s}^{- 1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In an ideal gas at temperature $T$, the average force that a molecule applies on the walls of a closed container depends on $T$ as ${T}^{q}$. A good estimate for $q$ is
questions.solution:
The pressure exerted by molecules of a gas on the walls $p = \dfrac{1}{3}nm{c}^{2}$

$∴ p ∝ {c}^{2}$

But $C ∝ \sqrt{T}$ and ${C}^{2} ∝ T$

$∴ P ∝ T$

$∵$ Force $= P \times A$

$∴ F ∝ {T}^{1}$

$q = 1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The temperature at which a & molecule of nitrogen will have the same rms velocity as a & molecule of oxygen at $127 ° C$& is&
questions.solution:
Root mean square velocity

${v}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$

where $R$ is gas constant, $T$ the temperature and $M$ molecular weight.

Given, ${MN}_{2} = 28, {MO}_{2} = 32, {TO}_{2} = 127℃ = 127 + 273 = 400$ K

$∴ \dfrac{{{v}_{O}}_{2}}{{{v}_{N}}_{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{{T}_{O}}_{2}}{{{M}_{O}}_{2}} \times \dfrac{{{M}_{N}}_{2}}{{{T}_{N}}_{2}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{400}{32} \times \dfrac{28}{{{T}_{N}}_{2}}} = 1$

$⇒ {TN}_{2} = 350K = 77℃$.
